title: Density and Locale-aware Cost Card Accessibility Review
creator: Ava Gupta
description: Review and finalize accessibility and internationalization requirements for the new density toggle and locale-aware number formatting on Cost Cards and Dashboard list views. Goals: ensure compact and comfortable density modes meet WCAG 2.1 AA for keyboard/voiceover users, provide readable and locale-correct number formats (short/long) across locales, and validate color scales for contrast and color-blind safe palettes used in heatmaps and mini sparklines.
acceptance_criteria: Density toggle (Compact / Comfortable) is keyboard accessible and operable via space/enter with visible focus ring
All Cost Card numeric formats support both short (1.2K) and long (1,234) styles by locale and expose user preference via aria-label for screen readers
Contrast ratios for primary, secondary, and heatmap color tokens >= 4.5:1 for text and >= 3:1 for non-text where applicable; alternative high-contrast tokens exist
RTL layout flips timelines, sort indicators, and keyboard focus order without breaking reading order or aria-live announcements
Chart legends and sparklines provide textual descriptions in aria-hidden=false elements or offscreen descriptions that convey current value and delta
Automated Playwright + AXE checks cover the main density and locale permutations and are green in CI for target locales: en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-EG
qa_steps: Open Dashboard > Cost Cards in en-US and switch density to Compact; tab through each interactive control and confirm focus order (density toggle, dropdowns, row links)
Change browser locale to fr-FR and verify short/long number toggle displays localized separators and short units (e.g., 1,2 k vs 1,2K) and screen reader announces full value via aria-label
Enable RTL (ar-EG) and walk keyboard flows; confirm timeline arrows flip and table column headers announce sort direction with arrow key interactions
Run NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS) on a cost card with a heatmap; verify legend and value descriptions are announced; check aria-live updates for rollout state changes
Run Playwright accessibility snapshots for compact/comfortable, en-US and ja-JP, and attach AXE reports to the ticket
comments: 2025-02-18 Ava Gupta: Initial spec added. Prototype includes a density toggle and a short/long number display option. Figma prototype linked. Requesting engineering feasibility review for number formatting perf impact.

2025-02-20 Liam Carter (Eng): Spike complete — i18n helper can support localized short formats but needs a small mapping table for CLDR short units. Perf impact negligible. Suggest exposing format preference via user profile or console query param.

2025-02-22 Sofia Martinez (Design): Updated prototype with accessible toggle (role=switch) and explicit aria-labels for both density and number format controls. Added offscreen textual descriptions for mini-charts.

2025-02-25 Accessibility review (internal): NVDA tests pass basic flows; found two issues — focus ring suppressed in compact row collapse (WCAG 2.4.7 focus-visible) and heatmap contrast below 3:1 in mid-range colors. Proposed fixes: unify focus token, introduce high-contrast heatmap palette.

2025-02-27 Localization team: Requested additional locales (pt-BR, ko-KR). Noted pluralization edge cases for Japanese short units. Agreed to consult CLDR short patterns and defer translated microcopy to i18n owners.
decision_log: Use a role=switch implementation for the density toggle to ensure correct semantics across screen readers
Implement both short and long number formatting; default to short for condensed views but expose long in aria-label for SRs
Introduce a color-blind safe palette and a user preference override for high-contrast mode rather than changing default brand tokens
Defer per-locale microcopy translations to the i18n infra team; design will supply token keys and example strings
follow_up_tasks: ENG-3921: implement CLDR-based short unit mapping and add locale test vectors
ENG-3999: ensure focus-visible token is applied in compact collapsed rows (QA + unit tests)
PM-211: add density & number-format preferences to user settings roadmap
DES-7620: visual QA pass for heatmap palettes including protanopia/deuteranopia simulations
notes: Edge case: very large numbers in non-Western locales may require explicit rounding policy to avoid large RTL punctuation clusters. Recommend a short-term mitigation of truncation with tooltip exposing full localized value.
testing_matrix: Screen readers: NVDA (Windows), JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS, iOS), TalkBack (Android)
Browsers: Chrome, Safari, Firefox (desktop and mobile emulation)
Locales: en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, ja-JP, ar-EG, pt-BR, ko-KR
